title: Long Ago and Yesterday
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the four log lines. Answer out loud.
text: Four lines from the ship log. Line What it says 1 Sailors crossed this ocean in wooden ships with cloth sails, hundreds of years ago. 2 Yesterday the crew drew a new map of the cove. 3 People found their way at sea by the stars, long before there were maps like ours. 4 This morning a crew member checked the weather on the radio. How do we know about the sailors of long ago? Four kinds of thing tell us. An artifact is an object they left behind, like a brass compass in a museum case. A photograph shows what something really looked like. An interview is what you learn by asking somebody who was there, or whose family was. A document is something written down at the time, like a ship log or a letter. All four of those are primary sources. A book somebody wrote later, after reading the logs, is a secondary source.

She spent years teaching science to young people. She wrote books for them. She wanted girls to know something. They could do this work too.

title: Someone Who Made a Difference
dir: Listen while your teacher reads about her. Answer out loud.
text: Marie Curie grew up in Poland. At that time girls there were not allowed in. The universities would not take them. She saved for years. She moved to France. She studied science there. She was living on almost nothing. With her husband she worked in a shed. It was cold and leaky. She stirred heavy pots of rock. She did it for months on end. She found two new materials. Nobody had known about them. She was the first woman ever to win it. The Nobel Prize went to her. Then she won a second one. In a war she drove vans. They were fitted with machines. She had helped make them. So doctors could see inside. They could see a hurt arm or leg. Then they could set it properly.
